headline: Target comps up 3.8% on 3.6% traffic gain; $994M tariff refund lifts EPS to $4.11 and FY outlook raised again.
guidance_note: FY26 net sales growth raised to ~5% (from ~4%); GAAP/adj EPS $9.90-10.90 incl. ~$1.65 of Q2 tariff refunds; op margin ~6% incl. ~90bps refund benefit.
key_messages: Comparable sales +3.8% (stores +2.7%, digital +8.7%), driven almost entirely by a 3.6% rise in comparable traffic.
Gross margin 33.7% vs 29.0%: 3.7pts came from $994M IEEPA tariff refunds; underlying rate up ~100bps on lower markdowns, ads and non-merch growth.
EPS $4.11 vs $2.05 includes $1.65 from refunds; underlying EPS growth roughly 20%.
Target is reinvesting refunds in price: CFO Jim Lee said 'We have and will continue to invest in price'; >10,000 items already cut.
Food & beverage, beauty and toys lead; management says home and apparel still lag expectations, with home a multiyear fix.

consumer.big_ticket: Home and apparel, Target's highest-margin discretionary categories, still lagging the rest of the business per management.
consumer.pricing: Booked ~$994M of IEEPA tariff refunds; plans to keep investing in lower prices rather than refund shoppers directly.
consumer.quote: We have and will continue to invest in price. (CFO Jim Lee)

macro_read: Traffic-led growth at a mid-tier discretionary retailer shows shoppers still spending, but strength skews to food and consumables while home lags. Tariff refunds give retailers room to cut prices, a mild disinflationary impulse for goods.

sources.label: Modern Retail: Target tariff refunds, plans to lower prices
TIKR: Q2 call food vs home gap

notes: EPS of $4.11 includes $1.65 of one-time IEEPA tariff refunds; $2.46 without them. The beat is measured on $2.46.
